route: Free search: THE VALUE ALPHABET. I parameterised SSG-Value by the *set of numbers* the value vector takes -- Lambda(G) = {val(v)}, k(G) = |Lambda(G)|, D(G) = the least common denominator -- which is the "number of distinct values" starting point offered in the brief and is not any anti-list item (the anti-listed parameters -- a, escape exponent, transversal, treewidth, k-acyclicity, matrix rank, escape certificates -- are all properties of the PRESENTATION; k and D are properties of the value and are invisible in the graph). The route delivered: (i) an exactness theorem for iteration on any grid containing the values, valid on arbitrary SSGs, whose proof is one line of thm:lfp-general(b); (ii) a rigidity theory of the alphabet (a covering lemma by lem:trapchar, a sharp denominator bound D <= 2^{k-2} via lem:watched, a complete classification for k <= 4); (iii) a new polynomial class {D <= poly(N)} that strictly refines thm:few-avg and is not contained in the escape class. NOTE ON THE ANTI-LIST: the ALGORITHM in fvb:cor-grid is a rounded value iteration, and value iteration is anti-listed. I am flagging this rather than hiding it. The content is not an analysis of value iteration's rate: it is that the UP-rounded operator's least fixed point is exactly val on a finite lattice (the down-rounded one is false, with an explicit witness), plus the two rigidity theorems that bound the lattice's size against k. If the root agent judges the algorithmic corollary to fall under the anti-list, the rigidity results (fvb:lem-cover, fvb:thm-rigid, fvb:thm-den, fvb:thm-k4, fvb:cor-chain, fvb:prop-fv) stand independently of it.
headline: val is the LEAST fixed point of the UP-rounded Shapley operator on any finite grid containing it (arbitrary SSGs, from thm:lfp-general(b) in one line; the down-rounded version is false, 5-vertex witness); on stopping games the value alphabet is rigid -- every interior value is the midpoint of two others, else its class is a trap -- forcing a single common denominator D <= 2^{k-2}, sharp, so val is computable in O(N^2 D^2) <= O(N^2 4^k) and {D <= poly} is a new polynomial class strictly containing {a <= log N} and not contained in the escape class (family FV_2 with k=4, D=3, a=Theta(N) and every escape certificate exponentially bad). The class does not reach the frontier: on L_n, H_m, G_m, WD and CC the measured k equals 2 + log_2 D exactly, so k = Theta(N) there.

results.name: fvb:thm-alph (Alphabet iteration is exact)
results.statement: Let G be an SSG, stopping or not, and Lambda any finite subset of [0,1] containing every value of G. Let ceil_Lambda(t) = min{mu in Lambda : mu >= t} and Psi(x) = ceil_Lambda(Tx) with the sinks pinned. Then the iterates x_0 = bottom, x_{t+1} = Psi(x_t) increase and reach val after at most N(|Lambda|-1)+1 steps; val is computable in O(N^2 |Lambda| log|Lambda|) operations.
results.argument: Lambda^V with sinks pinned is a finite complete lattice; Psi is monotone (T monotone, ceil nondecreasing) and maps it to itself since 1 in Lambda. val is IN the lattice and T val = val, so Psi(val) = val; hence the increasing iterates from the bottom stay <= val and stabilise at some c <= val with c = Psi(c). Then c = ceil_Lambda(Tc) >= Tc, i.e. c is in X with Tc <= c, and thm:lfp-general(b) says val = min{x in X : Tx <= x} with NO stopping hypothesis, so val <= c. Hence c = val. Each productive sweep raises one coordinate one letter, and each of N coordinates can rise |Lambda|-1 times.
results.verification: kval.py/grid.py/t_grid.py/t_final.py/recheck.py, exact Fractions. 600 random games (99 stopping, 501 not) at n=4..10: 0 mismatches, and multiples 2D also work. 200 fresh larger games n=14..26 (109 NON-stopping): 0 mismatches. 600 further fresh games n=5..19 with seeds disjoint from all earlier runs: 0 failures. Also confirmed on L_n, H_m, G_m, WD, CC, GR, FV up to N=502.

results.name: fvb:rem-down (the downward rounding is false)
results.statement: The least fixed point of x -> floor_Lambda(Tx) from the bottom is NOT val: on the 5-vertex stopping game Vavg = {0,2,3,4}, Vmin = {1}, 0->(3,t0), 1->(t0,t1), 2->(2,4), 3->(4,2), 4->(t1,0) one has val = (1/3, 0, 2/3, 2/3, 2/3) while the downward iteration halts at (0,0,0,0,1/3).
results.argument: A fixed point of floor_Lambda(T .) satisfies only c <= Tc, which by thm:lfp-general bounds c above by the greatest fixed point and below by nothing; the direction of the rounding is the whole content of fvb:thm-alph.
results.verification: kval.py seed 2, exact Fractions; the same run found 138 downward and 127 upward-from-the-top mismatches in 300 random games. The instance also shows values need NOT be dyadic (denominator 3), correcting a first-pass case analysis of mine.

results.name: fvb:cor-grid (grid iteration)
results.statement: If D is any positive integer with D*val(v) integral for all v, then val is computed by at most DN+1 sweeps of x -> ceil_D(Tx) from the bottom, all intermediate quantities being integers in [0,D].
results.argument: fvb:thm-alph with Lambda = (1/D)Z cap [0,1]; on that grid ceil_D of a mean is ceil((i+j)/2)/D, so a sweep is O(N) integer operations.
results.verification: as above; measured sweep counts are far below the DN bound on every family (table in fvb:rem-measure).

results.name: fvb:lem-cover (covering lemma)
results.statement: In a stopping SSG, every interior value lambda (0 < lambda < 1) is attained at some average vertex whose two successors have DIFFERENT values; consequently lambda = (lambda_i + lambda_j)/2 for two other letters lambda_i < lambda < lambda_j of the alphabet.
results.argument: Let S = {v : val(v) = lambda}; it is nonempty and sink-free. If no average vertex of S mixes then every average vertex of S has BOTH successors in S, and every controlled vertex of S has SOME successor in S (the arg max / arg min). By lem:trapchar S is a nonempty trap, contradicting stopping.
results.verification: t_cover.py and recheck.py: 0 failures on 800 + 600 random stopping games (exact arithmetic). It also predicts non-realisable alphabets, e.g. no stopping SSG has value set {0,1/8,1/4,1/2,7/8,1}; 18 of the 148 pinned alphabets at k=6 and 660 of the 2154 at k=7 are deleted this way.

results.name: fvb:thm-rigid (rigidity of the alphabet)
results.statement: For a stopping SSG with k distinct values there is a choice, for each interior index l, of i_l < l < j_l with lambda_{i_l} + lambda_{j_l} = 2 lambda_l such that the system lambda_l = (lambda_{i_l}+lambda_{j_l})/2 (2 <= l <= k-1), lambda_1 = 0, lambda_k = 1 has Lambda(G) as its UNIQUE solution. Hence at most C(k,2)^{k-2} <= k^{2k} sets occur as the alphabet of a stopping SSG with k values, and the list is computable from k alone.
results.argument: fvb:lem-cover gives the choice, one equation per interior letter. Writing it as (I-P)lambda' = b, P >= 0 has row sums <= 1. If rho(P) = 1 some nonempty U of interior indices has P[U,U] stochastic; taking l = min U, row l puts both halves in U, so i_l in U with i_l < l = min U, a contradiction. So rho(P) < 1, I-P is nonsingular, the solution is unique, and Lambda(G) solves it.
results.verification: lamenum.py enumerates all pinned alphabets: 1,1,3,16,148,2154 for k=2..7. t_struct.py confirms that in every case where the covering lemma is satisfiable a nonsingular one-equation-per-class system exists (130/130 at k=6, 1494/1494 at k=7).

results.name: fvb:thm-den (denominator against the alphabet, sharp)
results.statement: A stopping SSG whose value vector takes k distinct values has a single common denominator D(G) <= 2^{k-2}; equivalently k(G) >= 2 + log_2 D(G). The bound is attained by the ladder L_n (k = n+2, D = 2^n).
results.argument: From fvb:thm-rigid, lambda' = (2I-2P)^{-1}(2b) with 2I-2P integral and 2b in {0,1}^{k-2}. lem:watched gives 0 < det(I-P) <= 1, so det(2I-2P) = 2^{k-2} det(I-P) is a positive integer <= 2^{k-2}; Cramer makes every lambda_l an integer over that determinant, so D(G) divides det(2I-2P). Sharpness by back-substitution on L_n.
results.verification: t_cover.py: max |det(2I-2P)| over ALL one-per-class systems equals exactly 2^{k-2} for k=3..7 (2,4,8,16,32). 800 + 600 + 200 random stopping games: 0 violations of D <= 2^{k-2}, with the ratio D/2^{k-2} reaching 1.

results.name: fvb:cor-fewvals (the polynomial class)
results.statement: The value vector of a stopping SSG is computable in O(N^2 D(G)^2) arithmetic operations -- run fvb:cor-grid for D = 1,2,3,... and return the first x with Tx = x -- hence in O(N^2 4^k). The stopping SSGs whose values have a common denominator polynomial in N, among them all those taking O(log N) distinct values, are decidable in polynomial time.
results.argument: At D = D(G) the iteration returns val, a fixed point of T, so the loop halts at some D <= D(G); whatever D it halts at, the output is a fixed point of T, and on a stopping game that fixed point is unique (cor:comparison), so the output is val. Cost sum_{D <= D(G)} O(DN^2).
results.verification: t_final.py: on every stopping instance with D <= 48 among 200 fresh games on 14--26 vertices, the search returned val at exactly D = D(G); 0 algorithm errors.

results.name: fvb:rem-compare (strict refinement of thm:few-avg)
results.statement: D(G) <= 2^{min(a, k-2)}, so fvb:cor-grid never loses to thm:few-avg and strictly wins on the paper's own instances: H_m has a = 2m+1 but D = 2^{m+1}, G_m has a = 2m but D = 2^{m+1}. The two parameters are exponentially far apart in general (fvb:prop-fv: stopping games with a = Theta(N) and k = 4, D = 3).
results.argument: D <= 2^a is lem:denominator-sharp; D <= 2^{k-2} is fvb:thm-den; the measurements supply the separating instances.

results.name: fvb:thm-k4 (classification of small alphabets)
results.statement: The value set of a stopping SSG with at most four distinct values is one of {0,1}, {0,1/2,1}, {0,1/4,1/2,1}, {0,1/3,2/3,1}, {0,1/2,3/4,1}; all five occur, and such a game is solved by at most 4N+1 sweeps with D in {1,2,3,4}.
results.argument: By fvb:lem-cover each interior letter is the midpoint of a straddling pair; for {0,lambda,mu,1} the only straddling pairs are (0,mu),(0,1) for lambda and (lambda,1),(0,1) for mu, giving four combinations of which lambda = mu = 1/2 violates lambda < mu; the other three give (1/4,1/2), (1/3,2/3), (1/2,3/4). Realised by v->(t0,t1), by the game of fvb:rem-down and FV(n), by L_2, and by the dual of L_2 (lem:duality).
results.verification: t_kfour.py / t_kfour_big.py / recheck.py: on 1379 + 400 + 600 random stopping instances with k <= 4 no alphabet outside the list ever appeared, and all five appeared. A separate attractor-plus-monotone-propagation procedure for k <= 4 (kfour.py, complete by a trap argument) also solved 1379/1379 with 0 unsound answers; it is subsumed by fvb:cor-grid and is kept only as code.

results.name: fvb:prop-fv (four values, a = Theta(N), outside the escape class)
results.statement: FV(n) (X_i in Vmax -> (L_i,L_{i+1}), Y_i in Vmin -> (M_i,M_{i+1}), L_i in Vavg -> (t0,Y_{i+1}), M_i in Vavg -> (t1,X_{i+1}), i in Z_n) is stopping with N = 4n+2, a = 2n, both players, val = 1/3 on X,L and 2/3 on Y,M, so k = 4 and D = 3; all n Max vertices lie in one SCC of the Max-reachability digraph, so thm:bounded-components gives only 2^n - 1. FV_2(n), which hangs a survival chain C_i -> (C_{i+1}, C_0), C_{n-1} -> (L_0, C_0) off X_0 -> (L_0,C_0), has the same four values with N = 5n+2, a = 3n, and every escape certificate (lambda,x) satisfies (a + log kappa)/log(1/lambda) >= 2^{n-1}.
results.argument: The displayed vector is a fixed point of T and no nonempty trap exists (L_i and M_i have a sink successor, then X_i and Y_i lose both/some, then the chain collapses from C_{n-1}), so it is val by cor:comparison. For the escape bound: q_t := (S^t 1)(C_0) <= lambda^t kappa by homogeneity, while q_t >= 1 - t 2^{-n} because leaving the chain requires being at C_{n-1}, which requires the previous n-1 flips to agree; t = 2^{n-1} gives 1/2 <= lambda^t kappa, hence log(1/lambda) <= log(2 kappa)/2^{n-1}.
results.verification: fv.py and table2.py, exact: stopping, four values, D = 3, solved in 4 sweeps (FV) and 8/28/103 sweeps (FV_2 at n = 5,25,100, N up to 502). t_escape_fv.py measures the survival S^t(1) at C_0: 0.945, 0.888, 0.785, 0.613 at t = 2^{n-3}, 2^{n-2}, 2^{n-1}, 2^n for n = 10, matching the bound. Max-SCC sizes measured as n for n = 5,6,7,9.

results.name: fvb:prop-extremes (both extremes of the denominator bound)
results.statement: The gambler's ruin chain GR(n) (u_i in Vavg -> (u_{i-1}, u_{i+1}), u_0 = t0, u_{n+1} = t1) is stopping with val(u_i) = i/(n+1), so k = n+2 and D = k-1, the least possible; fvb:cor-grid runs in O(N^3) although a = Theta(N). The ladder L_n has the same k and D = 2^{k-2}. So D, not k, is the parameter the algorithm sees, and the two are exponentially far apart on realised families.
results.argument: Direct back-substitution plus uniqueness of the fixed point on a stopping game; the denominator of an alphabet of size k is at least k-1 because the k letters lie in (1/D)Z cap [0,1].
results.verification: gr.py: GR(3),GR(5),GR(8),GR(12) give (k,D) = (5,4),(7,6),(10,9),(14,13) and the grid iteration returns val in 4,7,12,19 sweeps.

results.name: fvb:cor-chain (the alphabet is a small game's value vector)
results.statement: The value alphabet of a stopping SSG with k distinct values is the value vector of a PLAYER-FREE SSG on k-2 average vertices in which vertex l has one successor strictly below and one strictly above it, with letter 1 read as t0 and letter k as t1.
results.argument: The system of fvb:thm-rigid is exactly that chain's fixed-point equation, and rho(P) < 1 makes the chain stopping, so its value vector is the unique solution, namely Lambda(G).
results.verification: lamenum.py builds exactly these chains; the converse fails (both l=2 and l=3 pointing at (t0,t1) gives lambda_2 = lambda_3 = 1/2), so strict monotonicity must be checked, which the enumeration does.

results.name: fvb:rem-equiv (TARGET-EQUIVALENT reformulation -- flagged)
results.statement: SSG-Value is in P if and only if there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given G, outputs a set of rationals of polynomial cardinality containing every value of G.
results.argument: (<=) fvb:thm-alph solves G in O(N^2 |Lambda| log|Lambda|) once such a Lambda is in hand. (=>) the standard search-to-decision reduction outputs the exact value set. This is of the same strength as the target and must be read as such; its only content is a relocation of the difficulty -- to the manufacture of a candidate ALPHABET, with no assignment of letters to vertices, which is strictly less information than the guides of thm:order-determines and rem:bsi require.
results.verification: n/a (a reduction); the forward direction is exercised by every run of grid.py.

results.name: Measurement: k = 2 + log_2 D on every hard family
results.statement: On L_n, H_m, G_m, WD(e,j,m) and CC(L,m) the inequality k >= 2 + log_2 D of fvb:thm-den is an EQUALITY, so on the paper's hard families the alphabet carries exactly as much information as the denominator and no more; the gap opens only on instances built for it (FV, GR).
results.argument: Exact computation of val on each family, then k and the least common denominator.

results.name: Warning: WD degenerates at m = j+1
results.statement: The wedge WD(e,j,m) of def:wedge must be read at m > j+1: at m - j = 1 the w-chain collapses to w_1 -> (t0,t1) and WD(3,2,3) has val identically 1/2 off the sinks (k = 3, D = 2), solved in four sweeps.
results.argument: L = m-j = 1 takes the guard branch of the construction, which destroys the 2^{-m} gap the family exists to create.
results.verification: Direct exact computation of val on WD(3,2,3): every non-sink has value 1/2. At honest parameters WD(3,2,5), WD(4,3,6), WD(3,3,7) have D = 2^m and k = m+2 as intended.

gap: MISSING STATEMENT (one sentence, self-contained): "There is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a stopping SSG G on N vertices, outputs a finite set of rationals of cardinality polynomial in N that contains every entry of val." By fvb:thm-alph this statement is TARGET-EQUIVALENT -- it implies SSG-Value in P and is implied by it -- so the route's continuation is BLOCKED in the sense of rule 4, and I say so rather than presenting it as progress. Two weaker statements I could not settle and that are NOT known to be target-equivalent: (i) "every strictly increasing solution of an order-respecting midpoint chain on k-2 states is the value alphabet of some stopping SSG" (the covering lemma is necessary; sufficiency would give a complete characterisation of value alphabets, and would tell us the exact number of alphabets to search); (ii) "on every stopping SSG, k(G) = 2 + ceil(log_2 D(G))" -- FALSE as stated (the uniform alphabet {0,1/4,1/2,3/4,1} has k = 5, D = 4), but the measured equality k = 2 + log_2 D on L_n, H_m, G_m, WD, CC asks for a structural hypothesis under which it holds, which would collapse the two parameters on the hard side.

%%% route free-search-b : the value alphabet
%%% paste-ready; labels prefixed fvb:

\subsection{The value alphabet}\label{fvb:sec}

Everything in this section is a statement about the \emph{multiset of
numbers} that $\val$ takes, not about the presentation. Write
\[
  \Lambda(G):=\{\val(v):v\in V\}\subseteq[0,1],\qquad k(G):=|\Lambda(G)|,
\]
and let $D(G)$ be the least positive integer with $D(G)\cdot\val(v)\in\Z$
for every $v$. Since $\val(t_0)=0$ and $\val(t_1)=1$ we always have
$0,1\in\Lambda(G)$ and $k(G)\ge2$. We write
$\Lambda(G)=\{\lambda_1<\dots<\lambda_k\}$, so $\lambda_1=0$,
$\lambda_k=1$, and call $\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{k-1}$ the
\emph{interior} letters. Say an average vertex $v$ \emph{mixes} if
$\val(v^{(0)})\ne\val(v^{(1)})$.

\begin{definition}[Alphabet iteration]\label{fvb:def-alph}
For a finite $\Lambda\subseteq[0,1]$ with $1\in\Lambda$ let
$\lceil t\rceil_\Lambda:=\min\{\mu\in\Lambda:\mu\ge t\}$ and let
$\Psi_\Lambda(x):=\lceil Tx\rceil_\Lambda$ coordinatewise, with the sinks
pinned to $0$ and $1$. Let $\bot_\Lambda$ be the vector that is
$\min\Lambda$ off the sinks.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Alphabet iteration is exact]\label{fvb:thm-alph}
Let $G$ be an SSG, \emph{stopping or not}, and let $\Lambda$ be any finite
subset of $[0,1]$ with $\Lambda\supseteq\Lambda(G)$. Then the iterates
$x_0:=\bot_\Lambda$, $x_{t+1}:=\Psi_\Lambda(x_t)$ increase and reach
$\val$ after at most $N(|\Lambda|-1)+1$ steps. Hence $\val$ is computable
in $O\bigl(N^{2}|\Lambda|\log|\Lambda|\bigr)$ arithmetic operations once
such a $\Lambda$ is known.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$\Lambda^{V}$ with the sinks pinned is a finite complete lattice and
$\Psi_\Lambda$ is monotone on it, because $T$ is monotone and
$t\mapsto\lceil t\rceil_\Lambda$ is nondecreasing; it maps the lattice to
itself because $1\in\Lambda$. Since $\val\in\Lambda^{V}$ and
$T\val=\val$, we get $\Psi_\Lambda(\val)=\lceil\val\rceil_\Lambda=\val$:
$\val$ is a fixed point of $\Psi_\Lambda$. From $x_0\le\val$ and
monotonicity, $x_t\le\val$ for all $t$; from $x_0\le\Psi_\Lambda(x_0)$
and monotonicity the sequence increases, so it stabilises at some
$c\le\val$ with $c=\Psi_\Lambda(c)$.

Now $c=\lceil Tc\rceil_\Lambda\ge Tc$, so $c\in\mathcal{X}$ satisfies
$Tc\le c$, and \Cref{thm:lfp-general}(b) --- $\val=\min\{x\in\mathcal
X:Tx\le x\}$, with no stopping hypothesis --- gives $\val\le c$.
Therefore $c=\val$. Both inequalities are needed and each uses one half
of the construction: the iteration from below gives $c\le\val$, the
upward rounding gives $c\ge\val$.

For the count: each step that changes anything raises at least one
coordinate to the next letter of $\Lambda$, and each of the $N$
coordinates can be raised at most $|\Lambda|-1$ times.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}\label{fvb:rem-down}
The direction of the rounding is the entire content. The downward variant
$\lfloor Tx\rfloor_\Lambda$ is also monotone and also has $\val$ as a
fixed point, but its least fixed point $c$ satisfies only $c\le Tc$,
which bounds nothing from below; it is false. On the $5$-vertex stopping
game $\Vavg=\{0,2,3,4\}$, $\Vmin=\{1\}$, $0\to(3,t_0)$, $1\to(t_0,t_1)$,
$2\to(2,4)$, $3\to(4,2)$, $4\to(t_1,0)$ one has
$\val=(\tfrac13,0,\tfrac23,\tfrac23,\tfrac23)$ and
$\Lambda(G)=\{0,\tfrac13,\tfrac23,1\}$, while the downward iteration
halts at $(0,0,0,0,\tfrac13)$.
\end{remark}

\begin{corollary}[Grid iteration]\label{fvb:cor-grid}
Let $D$ be any positive integer with $D\cdot\val(v)\in\Z$ for all $v$
--- for instance any multiple of $D(G)$. Then $\val$ is computed by at
most $DN+1$ sweeps of $x\mapsto\lceil Tx\rceil_{D}$ from the bottom,
where $\lceil\cdot\rceil_{D}$ rounds up to the nearest multiple of $1/D$;
all intermediate quantities are integers below $D$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{remark}\label{fvb:rem-priorart}
\Cref{fvb:cor-grid} is a rounded value iteration and should be read as
folklore in the Markov-decision-process tradition until someone finds the
reference; the two-sided rounding of Haddad--Monmege is the nearest
published relative, and \Cref{thm:few-avg} reaches the same $2^{a}$ by
approximation plus a final rounding rather than by an exact lattice
fixed point. What is not folklore is the parameter: the bound is driven
by $|\Lambda|$, and \Cref{fvb:thm-den} below bounds $|\Lambda|$ against
$D$ in the opposite direction.
\end{remark}

\subsection{The alphabet is rigid}

\begin{lemma}[Covering]\label{fvb:lem-cover}
Let $G$ be stopping and let $\lambda$ be an interior letter of
$\Lambda(G)$. Then some average vertex of value $\lambda$ mixes.
Consequently there are letters $\lambda_i<\lambda<\lambda_j$ of
$\Lambda(G)$ with $\lambda_i+\lambda_j=2\lambda$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $S:=\{v:\val(v)=\lambda\}$; it is nonempty and, as
$0<\lambda<1$, contains no sink. If no average vertex of $S$ mixes then
every average vertex of $S$ has \emph{both} successors of value
$\lambda$, hence both in $S$. Every $v\in\Vmax\cap S$ has
$\val(v)=\max_i\val(v^{(i)})=\lambda$, so \emph{some} successor lies in
$S$, and dually at $\Vmin$. By \Cref{lem:trapchar} $S$ is a nonempty
trap, so $G$ is not stopping. The last sentence is the mixing vertex's
equation, the mean of two distinct values lying strictly between them.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Rigidity]\label{fvb:thm-rigid}
Let $G$ be stopping with $k=k(G)$. Then there is a choice, for each
interior index $l$, of indices $i_l<l<j_l$ with
$\lambda_{i_l}+\lambda_{j_l}=2\lambda_l$, such that the resulting linear
system
\[
  \lambda_l=\tfrac12\bigl(\lambda_{i_l}+\lambda_{j_l}\bigr)
  \quad(2\le l\le k-1),\qquad \lambda_1=0,\ \lambda_k=1,
\tag{$\ast$}
\]
has $\Lambda(G)$ as its \emph{unique} solution. Consequently the number
of subsets of $[0,1]$ that occur as $\Lambda(G)$ for a stopping SSG with
$k$ distinct values is at most $\binom{k}{2}^{k-2}\le k^{2k}$, and the
list is computable from $k$ alone.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
\Cref{fvb:lem-cover} supplies the choice. Write $(\ast)$ on the unknowns
$\lambda_2,\dots,\lambda_{k-1}$ as $(I-P)\lambda'=b$, where row $l$ of
$P$ carries $\tfrac12$ in column $i_l$ and in column $j_l$ whenever that
index is interior, and $b_l=\tfrac12$ if $j_l=k$ and $0$ otherwise. Then
$P\ge0$ has row sums at most $1$. If $\rho(P)=1$ then some nonempty
$U\subseteq\{2,\dots,k-1\}$ has $P[U,U]$ stochastic; let $l:=\min U$. Row
$l$ has both its halves inside $U$, so $i_l\in U$; but $i_l<l=\min U$, a
contradiction. Hence $\rho(P)<1$, $I-P$ is nonsingular, and $(\ast)$ has
a unique solution, which is $\Lambda(G)$ because $\Lambda(G)$ solves it.
The count is the number of choice functions $l\mapsto(i_l,j_l)$.
\end{proof}


\begin{corollary}[The alphabet is itself a small game's value]\label{fvb:cor-chain}
The value alphabet of a stopping SSG with $k$ distinct values is the value
vector of a \emph{player-free} SSG on $k-2$ average vertices $2,\dots,k-1$
in which vertex $l$ has one successor strictly below it and one strictly
above it, with $1$ read as $t_0$ and $k$ as $t_1$. Hence the candidate
alphabets of size $k$ are among the value vectors of the
$\le\binom{k}{2}^{k-2}$ order-respecting chains on $k-2$ states --- those
whose value vector happens to be strictly increasing, which is not
automatic (both $l=2$ and $l=3$ pointing at $(t_0,t_1)$ gives
$\lambda_2=\lambda_3=\tfrac12$) --- and the whole difficulty of
\Cref{fvb:rem-equiv} is that the chain is hidden.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
The system $(\ast)$ of \Cref{fvb:thm-rigid} is exactly the fixed-point
equation of such a chain, and $\rho(P)<1$ makes the chain stopping, so its
value vector is the unique solution, namely $\Lambda(G)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Denominators against the alphabet]\label{fvb:thm-den}
Let $G$ be stopping with $k=k(G)$ distinct values. Then
$D(G)\le 2^{\,k-2}$, and the bound is attained: the ladder $L_n$ of
\Cref{def:ladder} has $k=n+2$ and $D=2^{n}$. Equivalently
$k(G)\ge 2+\log_2 D(G)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
In the notation of \Cref{fvb:thm-rigid}, $\lambda'=(2I-2P)^{-1}(2b)$ with
$2I-2P$ integral, $2b\in\{0,1\}^{k-2}$. By \Cref{lem:watched},
$0<\det(I-P)\le1$, so $\det(2I-2P)=2^{k-2}\det(I-P)$ is a positive
integer at most $2^{k-2}$. Cramer's rule writes every $\lambda_l$ as an
integer divided by $\det(2I-2P)$, so $D(G)$ divides $\det(2I-2P)$.
Sharpness: on $L_n$ back-substitution gives $\val(w_i)=1-2^{-(n-i+1)}$
and $\val(v_i)=1$, so $\Lambda=\{0\}\cup\{1-2^{-j}:1\le j\le n\}\cup\{1\}$
and $D=2^{n}$.
\end{proof}

\begin{corollary}[Few distinct values]\label{fvb:cor-fewvals}
The value vector of a stopping SSG is computable in
$O\bigl(N^{2}D(G)^{2}\bigr)$ arithmetic operations: run
\Cref{fvb:cor-grid} for $D=1,2,3,\dots$ and return the first $x$ with
$Tx=x$. Since $D(G)\le2^{k-2}$ by \Cref{fvb:thm-den} this is
$O(N^{2}4^{\,k})$. In particular the stopping SSGs whose value vector
has a common denominator polynomial in $N$ --- among them all those
taking $O(\log N)$ distinct values --- are decidable in polynomial time.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
For $D=D(G)\le2^{k-2}$ the iteration returns $\val$, which satisfies
$Tx=x$, so the loop stops at some $D\le D(G)$; whatever $D$ it stops at,
the output is a fixed point of $T$, and on a stopping game the fixed
point of $T$ is unique (\Cref{cor:comparison}), so the output is $\val$.
The cost is $\sum_{D\le D(G)}O(DN^{2})=O(D(G)^{2}N^{2})$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Comparison of bounds]\label{fvb:rem-compare}
$D(G)\le2^{a}$ is \Cref{lem:denominator-sharp}, so
$D(G)\le2^{\min(a,\,k-2)}$ and \Cref{fvb:cor-grid} never loses to
\Cref{thm:few-avg}. It strictly wins on the paper's own instances: on
$H_m$ one has $a=2m+1$ but $k=m+3$, so the exponent drops from $2m+1$ to
$m+1$; on $G_m$, $a=2m$ and $k=m+3$. The two parameters are genuinely
different --- \Cref{fvb:prop-fv} gives stopping games with $a=\Theta(N)$
and $k=4$ --- and $k$ is a property of the value, not of the
presentation, so it is immune to \Cref{prop:a-presentation}.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[Alphabets for $k\le4$]\label{fvb:thm-k4}
The value set of a stopping SSG with at most four distinct values is one
of
\[
  \{0,1\},\quad\{0,\tfrac12,1\},\quad
  \{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12,1\},\quad\{0,\tfrac13,\tfrac23,1\},\quad
  \{0,\tfrac12,\tfrac34,1\},
\]
and all five occur. Consequently such a game is solved by at most $4N+1$
sweeps of \Cref{fvb:cor-grid} with $D\in\{1,2,3,4\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
$k\le2$ gives $\{0,1\}$. For $k=3$, $\Lambda=\{0,\lambda,1\}$ and
\Cref{fvb:lem-cover} forces $\lambda$ to be the mean of two smaller-and-larger
letters, necessarily $0$ and $1$; so $\lambda=\tfrac12$. For
$k=4$, $\Lambda=\{0,\lambda,\mu,1\}$ and the mean of two letters
straddling $\lambda$ can only be $\tfrac12(0+\mu)$ or $\tfrac12(0+1)$
(the pair $(\lambda,\mu)$ has its mean in $(\lambda,\mu)$, which contains
no letter, and likewise $(0,\lambda)$ and $(\mu,1)$); similarly $\mu$ is
$\tfrac12(\lambda+1)$ or $\tfrac12(0+1)$. \Cref{fvb:lem-cover} applies to
both interior letters, and the two resulting equations are independent by
\Cref{fvb:thm-rigid}, leaving
four combinations, of which $\lambda=\mu=\tfrac12$ is excluded by
$\lambda<\mu$ and the other three give
$(\lambda,\mu)\in\{(\tfrac14,\tfrac12),(\tfrac13,\tfrac23),(\tfrac12,\tfrac34)\}$.
Realisability: $\{0,\tfrac12,1\}$ on $v\to(t_0,t_1)$;
$\{0,\tfrac13,\tfrac23,1\}$ on \Cref{fvb:rem-down}'s game and on
$\mathrm{FV}(n)$; $\{0,\tfrac12,\tfrac34,1\}$ on $L_2$; and
$\{0,\tfrac14,\tfrac12,1\}$ on the dual of $L_2$ (\Cref{lem:duality}).
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Census and realisability]\label{fvb:rem-census}
Enumerating the systems $(\ast)$ over all $\binom{k}{2}^{k-2}$ choices
and keeping the strictly increasing solutions in $(0,1)$ gives
$1,1,3,16,148,2154$ candidate alphabets for $k=2,\dots,7$, with largest
denominator exactly $2^{k-2}$ in each case, matching
\Cref{fvb:thm-den}. \Cref{fvb:lem-cover} then deletes $18$ of the $148$
at $k=6$ and $660$ of the $2154$ at $k=7$ --- for instance no stopping
SSG has value set $\{0,\tfrac18,\tfrac14,\tfrac12,\tfrac78,1\}$, because
$\tfrac78$ is not the mean of two other letters. All five alphabets of
\Cref{fvb:thm-k4} were realised by random search, and on $1379$ random
stopping instances with $k\le4$ no other alphabet appeared.
\end{remark}


\begin{proposition}[Both extremes of \Cref{fvb:thm-den} occur]\label{fvb:prop-extremes}
Let $\mathrm{GR}(n)$ be the gambler's ruin chain: $\Vavg=\{u_1,\dots,u_n\}$,
$u_i\to(u_{i-1},u_{i+1})$ with $u_0:=t_0$, $u_{n+1}:=t_1$. It is stopping,
$\val(u_i)=i/(n+1)$, so $k=n+2$ and $D=n+1=k-1$, the least denominator any
alphabet of size $k$ can have; \Cref{fvb:cor-grid} therefore runs in
$O(N^{3})$ although $a=\Theta(N)$. The ladder $L_n$ has the same $k$ and
$D=2^{k-2}$. So $D$, not $k$, is the parameter that the algorithm sees, and
the two are exponentially far apart on realised families.
\end{proposition}

\begin{remark}[Measurements]\label{fvb:rem-measure}
Exact rational arithmetic throughout; $\val$ by brute force over all
positional pairs, or (for the large $\mathrm{FV}$ instances) certified by
$Tx=x$ together with stopping.
\[
\begin{array}{lrrrrr}
\text{family} & N & a & k & D & \text{sweeps}\\\hline
L_3,L_5,L_7 & 8,12,16 & 3,5,7 & 5,7,9 & 2^{3},2^{5},2^{7} & 3,5,7\\
H_2,H_3,H_4 & 8,10,12 & 5,7,9 & 5,6,7 & 2^{3},2^{4},2^{5} & 6,12,25\\
G_2,G_3,G_4 & 6,8,10 & 4,6,8 & 5,6,7 & 2^{3},2^{4},2^{5} & 5,11,24\\
\mathrm{WD}(3,2,5) & 18 & 14 & 7 & 2^{5} & 31\\
\mathrm{WD}(4,3,6) & 22 & 18 & 8 & 2^{6} & 66\\
\mathrm{WD}(3,3,7) & 21 & 17 & 9 & 2^{7} & 58\\
\mathrm{CC}(2,2),\mathrm{CC}(3,3) & 19,26 & 15,22 & 8,11 & 2^{6},2^{9} & 27,84\\
\mathrm{GR}(5),\mathrm{GR}(9) & 7,11 & 5,9 & 7,11 & 6,10 & 7,14\\
\mathrm{FV}(5),\mathrm{FV}(25),\mathrm{FV}(100) & 22,102,402 & 10,50,200 & 4 & 3 & 4\\
\mathrm{FV}_2(5),\mathrm{FV}_2(25),\mathrm{FV}_2(100) & 27,127,502 & 15,75,300 & 4 & 3 & 8,28,103
\end{array}
\]
On \emph{every} family the paper builds to be hard --- $L_n$, $H_m$, $G_m$,
$\mathrm{WD}$, $\mathrm{CC}$ --- the inequality of \Cref{fvb:thm-den} is an
equality, $k=2+\log_2 D$; the alphabet carries exactly as much information as
the denominator there and no more. The gap opens only on instances built for
it. One warning: at the degenerate parameters $m-j=1$ the wedge collapses
($\mathrm{WD}(3,2,3)$ has $k=3$, $D=2$, solved in four sweeps), so the
family must be read at $m>j+1$.

Correctness was checked on $1500$ random stopping games on $4$--$8$ vertices,
on $400$ fresh ones on $12$--$24$ vertices with up to $8$ controlled
vertices, and on $200$ further fresh ones on $14$--$26$ vertices of which
$109$ were \emph{not} stopping: zero mismatches between
\Cref{fvb:cor-grid} at $D=D(G)$ and $\val$, zero violations of
$D\le2^{k-2}$ and of $D\le2^{a}$, zero failures of \Cref{fvb:lem-cover} on
$800$ random stopping games, and, on every stopping instance with
$D\le48$, the search of \Cref{fvb:cor-fewvals} returned $\val$ at exactly
$D=D(G)$.

The denominators of the surviving alphabets of \Cref{fvb:rem-census}
range over $[k-1,2^{k-2}]$ for $k\le7$, both ends attained
(\Cref{fvb:prop-extremes}).
\end{remark}

\subsection{A four-value family with $a=\Theta(N)$ and no escape certificate}

\begin{definition}[$\mathrm{FV}(n)$, $\mathrm{FV}_2(n)$]\label{fvb:def-fv}
For $i\in\Z_n$ put
$X_i\in\Vmax$, $Y_i\in\Vmin$, $L_i,M_i\in\Vavg$ with
\[
  X_i\to(L_i,L_{i+1}),\quad Y_i\to(M_i,M_{i+1}),\quad
  L_i\to(t_0,Y_{i+1}),\quad M_i\to(t_1,X_{i+1}).
\]
$\mathrm{FV}_2(n)$ adds $C_0,\dots,C_{n-1}\in\Vavg$ with
$C_i\to(C_{i+1},C_0)$ for $i<n-1$, $C_{n-1}\to(L_0,C_0)$, and replaces
$X_0\to(L_0,C_0)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{proposition}\label{fvb:prop-fv}
$\mathrm{FV}(n)$ is stopping with $N=4n+2$, $a=2n$, both players present,
$\val\equiv\tfrac13$ on the $X_i,L_i$ and $\equiv\tfrac23$ on the
$Y_i,M_i$; so $k=4$, $D=3$ and \Cref{fvb:cor-grid} halts within $3N+1$
sweeps (measured: four, independently of $n$). Every $X_i$ reaches
$X_{i+2}$ and $X_{i+3}$ through $L_i,L_{i+1}$, so all $n$ Max vertices
lie in one strongly connected component of the Max-reachability digraph
(checked for $n=5,6,7,9$) and \Cref{thm:bounded-components} gives only
the bound $2^{n}-1$ there.
$\mathrm{FV}_2(n)$ has the same values with $N=5n+2$, $a=3n$, and in
addition every escape certificate $(\lambda,x)$ of \Cref{def:survival}
satisfies
\[
  \frac{a+\log\kappa(x)}{\log(1/\lambda)}\;\ge\;2^{\,n-1},
\]
so $\mathrm{FV}_2$ lies outside the escape class of
\Cref{thm:escape-class} while lying inside the four-value class.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The displayed vector is a fixed point of $T$:
$\tfrac12(0+\tfrac23)=\tfrac13$, $\tfrac12(1+\tfrac13)=\tfrac23$,
$\max(\tfrac13,\tfrac13)=\tfrac13$, $\min(\tfrac23,\tfrac23)=\tfrac23$,
and in $\mathrm{FV}_2$ also $\tfrac12(\tfrac13+\tfrac13)=\tfrac13$ along
the chain. Stopping: a trap contains no sink, so no $L_i$ and no $M_i$
lies in one, whence no $X_i$ or $Y_i$ does either; in $\mathrm{FV}_2$,
$C_{n-1}$ needs $L_0$, then $C_{n-2}$ needs $C_{n-1}$, and the chain
collapses. By \Cref{cor:comparison} the fixed point is $\val$.

For the escape bound, let $q_t:=(S^{t}\bbone)(C_0)$. $S$ is monotone and
positively homogeneous and $Sx\le\lambda x$ with $x\ge\bbone$ gives
$S^{t}\bbone\le S^{t}x\le\lambda^{t}x$, so $q_t\le\lambda^{t}\kappa(x)$.
On the other hand $S$ takes the maximum at controlled vertices, so
$q_t$ is at least the probability, under the pair that plays into the
chain, that the token has met no sink in $t$ steps. Inside the chain the
token leaves only through $C_{n-1}\to L_0$, and being at $C_{n-1}$ at a
given time requires the previous $n-1$ coin flips to have chosen the
first successor, so the probability of leaving within $t$ steps is at
most $t\cdot2^{-n}$; hence $q_t\ge1-t2^{-n}$. Taking $t=2^{n-1}$ gives
$\tfrac12\le\lambda^{t}\kappa$, i.e.\ $t\log(1/\lambda)\le\log(2\kappa)$,
and therefore
$(a+\log\kappa)/\log(1/\lambda)\ge 2^{n-1}(a+\log\kappa)/\log(2\kappa)
\ge2^{n-1}$ since $a\ge1$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{What the parameter cannot do}

\begin{remark}[Target-equivalence]\label{fvb:rem-equiv}
By \Cref{fvb:thm-alph}, SSG-Value is in \textsf{P} \emph{if and only if}
there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given $G$, outputs a set of
rationals of polynomial cardinality containing every value of $G$. The
converse direction is the standard search-to-decision reduction. This is
a target-equivalent reformulation and must be read as such: it says only
that the whole difficulty is the manufacture of a small candidate
alphabet, not of the assignment of letters to vertices --- which is the
one thing \Cref{thm:order-determines} and \Cref{rem:bsi} do not say,
since a guide there must order the vertices.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[The ceiling]\label{fvb:rem-ceiling}
The parameter cannot reach the frontier. On the ladder $L_n$ of
\Cref{def:ladder}, $k=n+2$ and $D=2^{n}$, so
\Cref{fvb:cor-fewvals} is exponential there; and any family whose values
separate at scale $2^{-\Theta(N)}$ has $D=2^{\Omega(N)}$, hence
$k=\Omega(N)$ by \Cref{fvb:thm-den}. The measurements of
\Cref{fvb:rem-measure} put $\mathrm{WD}(e,j,m)$ at $D=2^{m}$, $k=m+2$,
$H_m$ at $D=2^{m+1}$, $\mathrm{CC}(L,m)$ at $D=2^{6},2^{9}$ for $(2,2),(3,3)$; on all of them $k=2+\log_2 D$ exactly. Since $D\le2^{a}$
always, an algorithm polynomial in $N$ and $\log D$ would be a polynomial
algorithm outright, so the linear dependence on $D$ in
\Cref{fvb:cor-grid} is exactly what a solution must remove.
\end{remark}
